title: Stage the intended changes
summary: The staging area holds the changes you intend to put in the next commit. Add only the files you mean to include.
introduction: The staging area holds the changes you intend to put in the next commit. Add only the files you mean to include. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: The staging area holds the changes you intend to put in the next commit. Add only the files you mean to include.
The staged difference shows note.txt ready for the next commit. Reviewing it helps avoid accidental additions.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the file again and compare staged and unstaged differences.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: git add takes the current file content; later edits need another add if they belong in the commit.
For more detail later, use this [Git further reading](https://git-scm.com/docs/gittutorial).
